reason: Critical errors: (1) Options 'b' and 'c' are identical (both say '16 mm (5/8 inch)'). (2) The correct answer for copper-clad rods is 13 mm (1/2 inch) per PEC 250.52(a)(5), but NONE of the options includes this value. Replaced option 'b' with the correct value and removed the duplicate.

rationale.a: Incorrect. 9.5 mm is below the PEC minimum and would not provide adequate cross-sectional area for reliable fault current carrying capacity.
rationale.c: Incorrect. 16 mm is the minimum for galvanized ferrous rods, not copper-clad rods. Copper has superior conductivity so a smaller diameter is permitted.
rationale.d: Incorrect. 19 mm exceeds the minimum requirement and is unnecessarily large for copper-clad conductors.
rationale.correct: PEC Article 250.52(a)(5) specifies minimum 13 mm (1/2 inch) diameter for copper or copper-clad rods. This is smaller than the 16 mm requirement for ferrous rods because copper has superior electrical conductivity.
rationale.takeaway: Material type determines grounding rod minimum diameter: ferrous requires 16 mm (5/8 inch), copper-clad requires 13 mm (1/2 inch) minimum.
